claim: The assembly.jl map entry omits leaf_declarations, declarations_found, ASSEMBLY_FAMILY, LEAF_FAMILY and _OTHER_FAMILY (13-55), which supply ClassUnreadable's found and family lists, and _holds_components (80), which supplies its did-you-mean.
why: src/assembly.jl:13-55 and :80-89 define ASSEMBLY_FAMILY, LEAF_FAMILY, _OTHER_FAMILY, leaf_declarations, declarations_found and _holds_components, all unexported helpers feeding classify (:58-70). code_map.md:8-12 makes an entry a selective list of constructs, not an inventory, and names `classify`, which these serve. The G1b verifiers overturned CV1-005, CV1-008, CV1-027, CV1-090, CV1-124 and CV2-040 on the same ground, following trial row C14-011. | The map is not required to list private helpers.

claim: The input_faces and output_faces docstrings, and spec 13.3, say nothing of refusals. A component with no class is refused as ClassUnreadable or ClassMixed, and a bad wire declaration as IllegalWireEntry outside a build.
why: Probe '116 no class' => ClassUnreadable, '116 both' => ClassMixed, '116 bad wires' => IllegalWireEntry :bare_pair, from input_faces outside a build (src/assembly.jl:435-437 classify, :476-478 _check_wire_shape). Appendix C covers both. spec.md:15588-15589 says 'A face primitive called outside a build refuses the same way, at the empty path', and §8.5 (spec.md:3702-3709) makes the class refusals total over any component. docstring_rules.md rule 21 does not require a refusal paragraph. | The behaviour is covered by Appendix C and §8.5, so the docstrings' silence is no mismatch. Adding a refusal sentence to the two docstrings would be optional polish.

claim: The public fields Relative.D and .Φ, Absolute.Δt and .τ, and StateEvent.guard and .handler are stated nowhere. Spec 8.7, Appendix B and the docstrings give only the constructors. docstring_rules 6 says a struct with public fields lists them.
why: The fields are read only inside src/: Relative.D/.Φ and Absolute.Δt/.τ at src/structure.jl:337-342 and :396-399, StateEvent.guard/.handler at src/build.jl:839, :1285, :1292 and :1596. No doc, example or test reads them as API. test/test_executor.jl:159 reads an executor body, not a StateEvent. docstring_rules.md rule 6 applies to a struct 'whose fields are public', and nothing makes these fields public. Spec 8.7, Appendix B (spec.md:14976-14979) and the docstrings make the constructors the surface. | The claim assumes the fields are public, but nothing establishes that.

claim: x_projection docstring says it runs after each integration step, after each event handler fires, and at init! and overlay!.
why: src/model.jl:650-652: run_boundary! projects first. frame.jl:160-164 runs it after every step and :316 at each t* boundary. src/executor.jl:393-394 _fire_project! runs after each handler. init! (model.jl:333, boundary_zero!) and overlay! (model.jl:474) run a boundary. Probe '078': init! => 1, overlay! => 1, one frame under BS3 with h_max = 1/4 => 4 projections for 4 steps.

claim: The declare.jl map entry omits the Tier enum, tier_word and update_of (783-835), the _holding guard predicate (601), COMPONENT_PATH (1008), _tier_names (910) and _declares_workspace (878).
why: src/declare.jl:783-835 (Tier, tier_word, update_of), :601-602 (_holding), :878 (_declares_workspace), :910 (_tier_names) and :1008 (COMPONENT_PATH) are unexported internals. :781 says the enum is 'the build's internal answer, not an authoring surface'. code_map.md:8-12 makes entries selective, and the G1b verifiers overturned the helper-omission rows CV1-005, CV1-027, CV1-090 and CV2-040 on that ground.

claim: code_map.md (declare.jl entry) calls contract_at 'the one-arity contract_at'. The function takes (fn, comp, tier) and an optional scalar S, so it is not one-arity.
why: code_map.md:321 'the one-arity `contract_at`' names the declaration form it reads, not its own signature. The phrase dates from c5c6986f (D-263), which replaced the two-argument contract forms (u_types(c, T)) with one-arity declarations, the 'One arity on both tiers' of spec.md:3720. contract_at (src/declare.jl:794-799) reads the declaration as invoke_declaration(fn, comp), with one argument, on both tiers. | A reader could take the phrase as contract_at's own arity. A rewording such as 'contract_at, the reader of the one-arity contract declarations' would remove the doubt, but that is optional.

claim: A selection that names a selector and keeps nothing is the warning `EmptyFaceSelection`.
why: src/assembly.jl:636-641 raises EmptyFaceSelection through _warn! when one selector is given and it keeps nothing; src/diagnostics.jl:755 severity :warning. probe.jl '035 empty selection warning' -> [EmptyFaceSelection] on the build's warnings; '035 bare silent' -> [].

claim: declaration_error(path, why) and declaration_error(path, unknown, legal) exist as two shapes
why: No function named declaration_error exists in src. Its two sketched shapes map onto the two throws in src/assembly.jl:620-631: UnknownFaceSelection reason :multiple_selectors, and reason :unknown_names with names and candidates (the did-you-mean against the face list). | Read as a sketch stand-in, as spec_rules.md:79-80 allows ('sketches may be simplified'). The (path, why) shape omits the selectors-given payload that the real :multiple_selectors diagnostic carries. If the audit reads the line as naming a real function, the fix is to replace the two declaration_error lines with `throw(DiagnosticError(UnknownFaceSelection(...)))` comments.
